post.caption: This metal looks like wood grain. It is called mokume-gane, which means wood-grain metal, and swirling layers of differently colored metals make the pattern. Metalworkers in Japan developed it in the 1600s for sword fittings, and Denbei Shoami is usually credited with it. Makers stack thin metal sheets, then fuse them with heat and pressure, and typical layers are copper and silver, sometimes with gold. The block is carved or drilled to expose the layers, then hammered flat so the wood-grain pattern appears. Because each piece is hand-made, no two match exactly. Tiffany reportedly showed mokume silver at the 1889 Paris world's fair, and centuries later jewelers took it up for rings.
